new_value: June 10, 2026: AWS Graviton5 (3nm, 192-core, +25% vs Graviton4) GA in EC2 M9g/M9gd, purpose-built for agentic-AI CPU inference; Meta deploying 'tens of millions' of cores, Uber + Snowflake onboard.
headline: AWS lands first-party agentic-AI silicon: Graviton5 GA with Meta/Uber/Snowflake validation
so_what: Blunts our 'AWS rents its AI soul / Google owns the whole stack' line on the CPU-inference layer where agentic workloads now run. Reps must stop claiming AWS has no first-party agentic-inference silicon. Reframe Google's edge specifically to AI accelerators/TPU (training + matrix compute) vs CPU, and note Graviton5 has external hyperscaler validation (Meta tens-of-millions of cores) the way we cite Blackstone/TPU demand.

new_value: AWS shipped a production-agent stack at Summit NYC (June 17, 2026): AgentCore harness GA, managed Knowledge Base, native Web Search grounding, agent observability/A-B testing, WAF AI-bot monetization, plus previews of AWS Context (agent knowledge graph) and AWS Continuum (agentic security).
headline: AWS ships production-agent platform at Summit NYC, contesting Google's Vertex and Gemini Enterprise Agent edge
so_what: Reps can no longer position Bedrock as proof-of-concept-only against a more mature Google agent platform. Stop leaning on agent-platform maturity as a clean Vertex/Gemini win, and shift the contrast to where Google still holds: TPU inference economics and single-stack model ownership. Flag that AWS Context and Continuum are previews, not GA, when a buyer cites them.

old_value: Tracked AWS/Amazon capex was global only: Amazon guided to roughly $200B in 2026 capex, with no India-specific commitment tracked.
new_value: Amazon added $13B for India AI/cloud through 2030, lifting its 2026-2030 India AI/cloud plan above $21B and total five-year India commitment to $48B, expanding AWS capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad with Trainium and Bedrock.
headline: AWS commits an extra $13B to India AI/cloud capacity through 2030
so_what: In India deals, AWS can now answer capacity doubts with a fresh local-capacity commitment in Mumbai and Hyderabad. A Google rep leaning on AWS supply constraints should expect that counter and reframe to Google's own $15B Andhra Pradesh AI hub rather than concede regional capacity.

old_value: After January's ~15% hike, the p5e Capacity Block reservation ran about $4.975 per accelerator hour.
new_value: About 20% higher on July 1, 2026: P5e $5.97, P5 $5.191 and P6-B300 $14.04 per accelerator hour, across the main Nvidia GPU reservation families.
headline: AWS raises guaranteed GPU reservation prices about 20% on July 1, its second hike in six months
so_what: On any deal comparing reserved GPU capacity, our rep can now cite two AWS GPU reservation hikes in six months (about 15% then 20%) as AWS using scarcity to raise AI prices, and steer the buyer toward TPU economics and automatic sustained-use discounts before the July 1 increase lands. Buyers reserving capacity have under a week to lock current rates.

new_value: AWS launched a $1B Forward Deployed Engineering org that embeds thousands of engineers inside customers to ship production AI in weeks, the first hyperscaler to do so.
headline: AWS puts $1B behind a Forward Deployed Engineering org that embeds engineers to ship production AI in weeks
so_what: Stop pitching delivery muscle as a clean Google win. AWS now has a named $1B org that embeds engineers to ship production AI in weeks, so in delivery-led deals lead with TPU inference cost and 63% growth, and let the IBM joint practice back that up instead of carry the whole argument.

new_value: AWS made Secret Cloud for Industry generally available, letting cleared defense contractors run classified (IL6) workloads on AWS in days, with Northrop Grumman first and an up to $20M migration accelerator.
headline: AWS opens classified cloud to defense contractors: Secret Cloud for Industry ships GA, Northrop Grumman first, $20M in credits
so_what: In defense-industrial-base deals, concede the classified core. AWS can now stand up a Secret-classified (IL6) environment in days where Google has no equivalent, so compete on the unclassified analytics and AI workloads around it instead of contesting the classified piece.

new_value: AWS committed up to $1B in outcome-based migration credits (ICAMF) through October 2030 for the 18 US intelligence agencies under its existing C2E contract; the CIA confirmed it will use it.
headline: AWS dangles up to $1B in migration credits to pull the US Intelligence Community deeper into its cloud through 2030
so_what: In IC and federal deals, expect AWS to wave $1B in migration credits tied to its existing C2E contract, so do not fight on migration price. Counter on Gemini and TPU capability the credits cannot buy, and name the deeper single-vendor lock-in the program builds in.

new_value: Bedrock Agents Classic in maintenance mode, closed to new customers July 30, 2026 (frozen model catalog, no new features); one of ~20 services AWS moved to maintenance mode on June 30, 2026. New agent customers must start on AgentCore, GA June 17, 2026.
headline: AWS puts its flagship Bedrock Agents into maintenance mode, one of about 20 services retired in a single June 30 sweep
so_what: Changes how a rep answers the "Google kills products, you just retired Vertex AI" objection: concede Google's deprecation history, then show AWS closed its own flagship agent product to new customers this month and moved about 20 services to maintenance mode in one announcement, so product churn is not a Google-only risk. Also useful in agent-platform deals: new AWS agent projects now begin on AgentCore, which has been GA only since June 17.

new_value: On July 17, 2026 an AWS unit-pricing bug showed customers fake estimated bills up to trillions of dollars in Cost Explorer and the Billing Console; actual invoices were unaffected and AWS corrected the data by July 18 noon PT.
headline: AWS billing console showed customers fake bills up to the trillions for a day
so_what: Gives reps a fresh, concrete data point when a buyer's FinOps or cost-control lead raises AWS billing unpredictability. Keep it honest: no real charges landed, so use it as evidence of operational fragility in the billing stack, not as an overcharge story.

new_value: AWS US-WEST-2 (Oregon) routing failure knocked Apple Pay, DoorDash, Reddit, Hulu, PSN and Twitch offline for about an hour on July 24, 2026; restored by 4:59 AM PDT.
headline: AWS Oregon region outage takes Apple Pay, DoorDash, Reddit and PSN offline for an hour
so_what: When a buyer cites Google's 2025 outage to argue AWS is the safer, more reliable default, the rep now answers with a concrete recent counter: AWS took Apple Pay, DoorDash, PSN and Reddit offline for an hour on July 24, so uptime is not a reason to default to AWS. Single region and about an hour, so it is a talking point for the reliability objection, not yet a deal-moving event.
